newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Empire East sets 2.0 to 2.5 bln peso capex.
newsitem.headline: Empire East sets 2.0 to 2.5 bln peso capex.

text.p: Mass housing developer Empire East Land Holdings Inc has budgetted 2.0 to 2.5 billion pesos as its capital expenditure for this year, chairman Andrew Tan told stockholders on Friday.
He did not say where the company would source the funds.
Buthe added the company has decided to defer the issuance of long-term and short-term commercial paper.
Late last year, the company had said it planned to issue up to three billion pesos in commercial paper.
"The board decided to defer the issuance. I think the timing is not good, and the market situation is not good," Tan said.
The company has been hit by persistent market rumours of financial difficulties, which company officials had vehemently denied.
Empire's shares fell 1.10 pesos to 4.70 pesos in early Friday trade after two days of steady climb. Traders attributed it to profit-taking.

Tan said the first quarter financial statement was not yet available, although he said he was expecting a 33 percent growth in its net profit this year from 1.57 billion pesos in 1996, and a 10 percent growth in revenues from 5.86 billion pesos in 1996.
